note: L2 curated catalog. Deterministic match, curated content. Every entry is offline-verifiable from this repo's research docs; URLs only from the public docs Research-found additions at suggest time are candidates: verifiedAt null.

entries.note: Extract PDF text with a CLI before it enters context. Use pdftotext for plain text, and pdfplumber when tables matter. This follows the public docs: one default, not a menu.
Slice large JSON at the source (jq '.field', jq -r). Do not read the whole file into context. The public docs give the same pipe-through guidance (head, grep, jq).
ripgrep is the tool for repeated grep or find loops over a tree. It is fast and gitignore-aware, and it produces bounded text evidence that a later proposal can verify.
When the repeated search is structural (find every call site / pattern in code, not a string), ast-grep matches the syntax tree instead of text.
Never paste spreadsheet content into context. Commit a small script that extracts the needed sheet or cells once, and run it again when needed. Then the session reads a short text result.

entries.feature: stable tool prefix (MCP pruning / deferred tools)
entries.note: cache_miss_reason tools_changed: the tool-definition block is the start of the cached prefix. When an MCP server connects, reconnects or loads tools mid-session, the next request writes the whole context into the cache again. It does not read it back. Load MCP servers at session start, and remove the ones that churn. Deferred MCP tools (the default) do not disturb the cached prefix.

cache_miss_reason system_changed: the system prompt (core instructions, tool definitions, output style) should only change when the loaded tool set changes or the client upgrades. Hook-injected content that varies run-to-run re-writes the prefix. Keep hook additionalContext byte-stable (no timestamps or counters).

cache_miss_reason messages_changed: the cache matches the start of each request exactly, so a change to an earlier message invalidates everything after it. Avoid resuming one session in two terminals (messages interleave into one transcript). Keep one model during a session, because each model has its own cache. On most models, an effort change in a session also starts a fresh cache. On Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and on Fable 5.1 from Claude Code 2.1.260, the cache stays intact by default. This holds with an API key or a Claude subscription.

A file already in context does not need re-reading. Each redundant read is sent again as fresh input and then carried in every later request. Keep durable facts in auto memory / CLAUDE.md instead of re-deriving them, and use offset/limit reads on big files.

A deterministic command sequence that you type 4 or more times belongs in a committed script. Use repo scripts/ or a bundled script of a skill. Per the public docs, bundled scripts run without ever entering context. One script call replaces the whole repeated block.

You can send independent reads and searches as one parallel batch in a single message. You can also fan them out to subagents, whose contexts are discarded. Each serial turn with a single call takes a full model round-trip.

The baseline preamble (system prompt + tool definitions + CLAUDE.md + memory) is re-sent with every request for the whole session. Trim sections that never change an outcome. Move procedure that you rarely need into skills that load on demand.

MCP servers whose tools are listed but never called still add their definition tokens to every main-thread request. Remove or scope idle servers. Deferred tools stay out of the cached prefix until they are fetched.

After a long idle gap, a large resumed context can require a fresh cache write. Batch related work while context is reusable, or start a focused session after a long break. Verify the effect from the next session. Do not assume a saving.

Base64 attachments are carried in context at their full token weight. Extract the text or table with a CLI first (pdftotext/pdfplumber for PDFs, an in-repo script for spreadsheets) and attach the extraction instead.

For a recurring, broadly reusable capability, evaluate an existing skill before you create one. Propose a specific skills.sh or `npx skills find <query>` search for the user to run. Compare source reputation, repository evidence, and install count. Never install or fetch from the deterministic catalog runtime. Every discovered skill remains a candidate until reviewed.

When repo or global evidence shows several related skills, agents, hooks, or MCP definitions must travel together, a plugin can package that set. A heavy skill alone is not enough evidence: confirm the related surfaces in the harness inventory before proposing packaging.

To give every subagent a default model, set the CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL environment variable. The model field of an agent file and the model of an Agent call win over that default, from Claude Code 2.1.251. The variable alone does not change the built-in Explore and Plan agents. To put every subagent on that one model, also set CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL_FORCE to 1 (Claude Code 2.1.257 or later).

entries.feature: a faster model for the search subagent
entries.note: Cursor runs its built-in Explore subagent on a faster model by default, so that it can run many searches in parallel. Its docs say to choose inherit when a subagent needs the same reasoning power as the parent. They also say to name a specific model when a subagent needs the capabilities of that model.

xAI lists low reasoning effort as the best fit for simple tool calling and for agent work where latency matters. Its reasoning models cannot turn reasoning off, so the effort level is the control. The usage of a request reports its reasoning tokens in their own field. Set a low effort on an agent or a skill that only calls tools.

Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 default to medium effort, and you cannot turn thinking off on them. On these models, the model decides at each step how much to think from the effort level. Use low for quick work that you review step by step. Keep max for hard work that runs without you, because max can overthink. If you set CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL, it wins over the effort of each skill and agent, so check it first.

OpenAI says that subagent workflows in Codex use more tokens than a comparable single-agent run. It advises subagents for read-heavy work, such as exploration, tests, triage and summaries, and more care with parallel edits. A subagent with no model or effort setting takes the model and effort of its parent.

entries.feature: subagents for parallel work and a fresh review
entries.note: Each subagent sends its own requests. A fresh subagent first gathers the context that your conversation already had, so it can be slower than the main thread. A subagent gives you parallel work or a reviewer with fresh eyes, not a better answer. Ask each subagent for a short summary, so that its results do not fill your context.

entries.tool: code that the agent writes to loop over tool calls
entries.note: Let the agent write code that calls the tools in a loop and filters the results. One run of that code replaces a chain of separate tool calls. By default, the intermediate results stay in the execution environment and do not enter the context of the model. The post covers MCP tools, and a script that loops over a repeated shell command works the same way.

entries.feature: a skill main file as a minimal router
entries.note: For a skill with several workflows, make its main file a minimal router that points to supporting docs and scripts. Then the skill does not force a read of the parts that the task does not need. Keep each skill description as short as possible, but clear about when to use the skill. OpenAI gives this advice for GPT-6 Astra in Codex.
